requirement:
When authoring evidence for a named example, its complete fenced declaration
MUST be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
The subject has one obligation. When authoring evidence for a named example, the example's complete fenced declaration MUST be in the mandatory input set. The wider rules for building and supplying that set belong to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, so I did not assess them here.

- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` prepares `AssessmentSources` for the example `requirements.case`.
  - It asserts the subject kind is `AssessmentKind::Definition(DefinitionKind::Example, false)`.
  - It asserts that `mandatory_inputs()[0]` has `requirements == "requirements.case"`.
  - It asserts that the input's `text` equals the full declaration exactly: the opening line `:::{example} case`, the body (which includes the cite and test roles), and the closing `:::`. This covers the "complete fenced declaration" wording, including the fence lines.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]` covers the `:::{example} case` form with citation roles in its body. For `guide.case`, `AssessmentSources::prepare` is run and the following are asserted:
  - `subject_text` contains the citation lines.
  - A mandatory input's text contains the citation lines.
  This shows that the preprocessing that hides citation metadata in the rendered book does not strip it from the declaration supplied as input.

Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. Together they check that the whole declaration is present in the input set, and that the input has the declaration's exact text. I found no unchecked obligation and no marking gap.
